utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Case number IT-97-25/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Mitar Rasevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will now ask for the appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the Prosecution we have Bill Smith, Christina Moeller, for case manager Diane Boles, and my name is Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have the appearances for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my name is Vladimir Domazet. I'm lead counsel for the accused Mr. Rasevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will ask the registrar to check that the accused can hear what is being said. Thank you. The Trial Chamber would like to greet everyone present in the courtroom; the representatives of the Prosecution, Defence counsel, the accused, as well as everyone else in this courtroom, in particular the interpreters, the registrar, the legal officer, and the usher as well. As you know, this is a Status Conference we are holding pursuant to Rule 65 bis. Yesterday there was a meeting with the legal officer who informed me of what will be discussed at the hearing. I was informed that there wouldn't be any particular problems, but I will give the floor to the Prosecution for them to tell me whether the disclosure according to Rule 66 and 68 is proceeding without any problems. Have all the documents or statements that the Prosecution has been provided -- have they all been provided to Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have disclosed all the materials that we currently have identified according to Rule 66 and Rule 68. In relation to the sensitive witnesses, we have disclosed the names to Defence counsel. We have not filed a protective measures motion yet, although we announced it during the last Status Conference, but we first wanted to await negotiations between the Defence and the Prosecution so that we actually can finalise our witness list. Only then it makes sense to request protective measures for the remaining witnesses. In relation to Rule 68, we have provided Rule 68 materials that came up in the Krnojelac case, and we will continue to do that. We have initiated general searches for this material, and after engaging in discussions with the Defence, we will fine tune these searches. The negotiations with the Defence we will start as soon as we have a final indictment, and both sides believe that we can agree on a lot of facts because we have actually already an appeal decision on the related case, the Krnojelac case. That is actually all I can say regarding to disclosure issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll address the issue of disclosure of documents again. Have all the documents in B/C/S -- or, rather, in English, have they been translated into English or have the documents in B/C/S been translated into English? I want to make sure there aren't any problems as far as the translations are concerned. Is translation progressing satisfactorily, and have you been able to disclose to Defence counsel all the translated documents?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and it was quite easy for us because we had actually all the documents used in the Krnojelac case, and so we had them already in B/C/S and English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the witnesses are concerned, yesterday you told the legal officer that it was your intention, roughly speaking, that you should have about 50 witnesses. Thirty-five witnesses would testify pursuant to 92 bis, Rule 92 bis, and 15 others would testify viva voce. So in fact, there wouldn't be many witnesses who would come to testify viva voce in the courtroom. As far as the witnesses who would be summoned to testify are concerned, you mentioned protective measures, and I'd like to remind both sides that many of these witnesses will certainly have already testified in another case. And as you know, if protective measures have already been granted to them, these protective measures shall still be in force unless a final decision has been made in the meantime. As in the Krnojelac case, the Appeals Chamber has already ruled this means that the protective measures are measures that the Trial Chamber will have to decide about, the Trial Chamber that is seized of the proceedings at present. I'll now turn to Defence counsel to ask him for his comments as far as the documents are concerned. Does he have all the documents? Has he come across any difficulties? Is the disclosure of documents proceeding as best as possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have received all the documents. I have no objections to raise and there are no problems as far as communicating with the OTP is concerned and as far as disclosure is concerned. Everything is fine for the moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Since everything is going well, we're very happy about that. In addition, and this was mentioned a while ago, a minute ago by the Prosecution, the parties are waiting for the Trial Chamber to render a decision which would be rendered following a motion filed by the Defence which concerns in particular three issues in the amended indictment. It concerns paragraph 2, paragraph 8, and the correspondence between paragraph 3 and 49. In the near future, the Trial Chamber will render its decision. We are about to finalise it, and a decision will be rendered very rapidly, which should enable both parties to have a better idea of the indictment. I assure you that this decision will be rendered before the end of the month. Given that there are no major obstacles, as the legal officer has informed you, in the course of September I intend to issue an order to fix or determine the future schedule for the hearings. As you are well aware, the Prosecution needs to establish a list of witnesses and exhibits, mention whether there are any agreements on certain issues, factual or legal issues, and in the course of the month of the September I will issue an order, and I believe that the trial could start, if no new problems arise, in the autumn of this year. This is what I wanted to inform you of because, as you know, the next hearing should be held in four months' time. It is July now, so that would be in October or in the month of November the case should be ready for trial. The only question is to know who will be trying the case. Since there are a number of trials which are being conducted at the moment, we might have a number of trials at the same time, but this doesn't depend on me. It's for the President and for the Registry to see when it will be possible to commence with the trial. At this point in time and with regard to this issue, is there anything the Prosecution would like to say? No?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, just given the fact that there's the summer break and people will be on vacation, the bulk of the negotiations that we will have with the Defence, and we have discussed it yesterday already, will actually take place in September. So I think we would need September for having these negotiations finalised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I'll now ask Mr. Rasevic about his health. Is everything fine? Do you have any health problems or is everything fine?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't have any health problems. I don't have any problems in the Detention Unit. I don't have any problems with the officials or with the other detainees. Everything is in order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. The conditions in the Detention Unit do not raise any objections on your part. Everything is okay.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The conditions are very good in the Detention Unit, and I have a very good treatment from the personnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you have visits? Do the members of your family visit you regularly?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In accordance with their circumstances, my family are visiting me, my wife and my children.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. You may be seated. Very well, then. Has the Prosecution got any questions to raise at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Domazet, do you have any questions to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, and there is nothing to raise at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This Status Conference has been very short. As far as the decision is concerned following the motion by the Prosecution, this will be rendered very soon, in September, as I have indicated. I will be able to announce the schedule for the autumn. I believe that it will be before November that we will see each other again because it has to be within the next four months. I wish you a good rest, and I will have the pleasure to see you next time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: at 9.15 a.m.
